feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by concrete platforms, scope, and outcomes. It is clear and polished overall, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, and it would be stronger with sharper prioritization and more quantified impact beyond activity descriptions.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression at NACo strongly support leadership in digital platforms, governance, and communications systems.  
- Good credibility signals: named tools, platform scale (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers), and recent project examples make the profile believable and substantive.  
- Writing is generally strong and professional, with consistent tone and effective use of action verbs.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and project descriptions; consolidate to improve scannability and avoid repeating Drupal, analytics, AI-enabled search, and multimedia themes.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics: e.g., efficiency gains, engagement lifts, search improvements, campaign performance, cost savings, or adoption results.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; punctuation/hyphenation varies (“front-end” vs. other compounds, “organization-wide,” “member-facing”); “French (A2/Learning)” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary.”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition and foreground the most marketable themes: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled discovery.
- Add scale or context from recent roles where possible (for example, high-volume public-sector platforms or large publisher environments) to increase impact.
- Replace “behind high-volume public-sector communications” with more direct, active phrasing.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web ecosystems for public-sector and advocacy organizations. Builds and leads governance models, analytics infrastructure, editorial operations, and multimedia systems that support high-volume publishing, cross-team coordination, and AI-enabled content discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle; vary the phrasing.
- The list of capabilities repeats core competencies almost verbatim; keep the intro higher-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating broad phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Cross-channel communications leadership”
- Replace generic terms with sharper, higher-value language: “AI-enabled search and structured content design” instead of “AI-enabled search and content experiences”
- Clarify operational depth: “Workflow automation and platform integrations” and “Multimedia production, livestreaming, and studio operations”
- Consider a more focused full rewrite: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and structured content design • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream, and studio operations”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “digital governance,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled search” already appear in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with multiple NACo roles; keep only if you want to foreground sector specialization.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently repeats several themes already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense for a footer. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or distinct scope will make it more impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use stronger, outcome-oriented verbs and specifics: e.g., “Created AI-powered legislative search with hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level chat for faster policy discovery.”
- Standardize style and punctuation across entries; “10×20-foot” is clear, but consider “10 x 20-foot” if matching the rest of the CV’s style.
- Replace generic phrases like “designed for continued campaign growth” with clearer value, such as “built for reuse and future campaign expansion.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with NACo experience bullets; keep footer versions shorter and more portfolio-like.
- “Editorial storytelling” and “production/distribution across website, email and social” echo existing communications language elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical range, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo roles and the Recent Projects section. Make it more “consulting-shaped”: emphasize advisory scope, selected high-impact deliverables, and any measurable outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery initiatives.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 3–4 outcome-oriented bullets; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one line about improving cross-channel communications operations.
- Replace generic phrasing (“deliver CMS development,” “advise on best practices”) with stronger verbs and outputs: “Built,” “launched,” “designed,” “streamlined,” “implemented.”
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages supported, toolkit downloads, publishing time reduced, search relevance gains, engagement or traffic improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital strategy, governance, workflows, analytics” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry; frame this role as post-tenure consulting and implementation support.
- Microsites and AI search are already echoed in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same detail in both places verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and distinguish strategic ownership here from execution-heavy responsibilities in the earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope-and-impact line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Recast bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable results where missing: growth in email engagement, social reach, production cost/time savings from the studio, reporting speed, or governance/compliance improvements.
- Combine channel oversight into one concise bullet and keep the strongest differentiators: enterprise web migration, analytics stack buildout, in-house studio launch, governance systems.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video-programming language overlaps with older NACo entries; emphasize building the studio and scaling in-house capacity instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Emphasize what changed under your ownership: scale, cadence, cross-team coordination, and channel-building.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day multi-channel digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video platforms, supporting advocacy and member engagement.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and distinct: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Recast internal-process bullets into one stronger line: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” overlaps with the later Director of Digital Media role; use “managed” or “oversaw” here to preserve progression.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it, unless that earlier item is revised.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the candidate’s senior-level positioning and emphasize governance/enterprise scope over broad communications phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, more distinctive wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and publishing systems
- Cross-channel communications operations
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications operations” to sound more concrete and less repetitive with leadership claims elsewhere.
- Change “Audience-focused content planning” to “Audience-centered content strategy” for a more senior, strategic tone.
- If space allows, add one higher-value qualifier such as “for high-volume public-sector organizations” to reinforce scale and fit.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the platforms/technical strengths most supported by recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a long list to a sharper, impact-oriented grouping: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or less evidenced items here, especially “WordPress,” “SharePoint,” “Power Pages,” and “jQuery,” unless they are central to target roles.
- Replace “Technical Execution” with “Web Platforms & CMS Delivery” or “Web Platforms & Technical Systems” to better match the CV’s modernization/governance narrative.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-linked: “Drupal platform delivery for large public-facing sites” or “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector websites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the detailed “Technical + IT” section; keep topline skills higher-level, not exhaustive.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so mention it only once if space is tight.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools for a senior digital leader, but this item reads like a raw keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. Make it more outcome-oriented and leadership-level.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + decision impact: “Analytics strategy, reporting and optimization” rather than “Analytics, Insights & Optimization.”
- Tighten and group terms: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” instead of listing in mixed order.
- Add higher-value phrasing: “KPI framework design,” “executive/leadership dashboards,” “performance and SEO analysis,” “conversion and content optimization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive reporting dashboards • SEO, content and conversion performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills strategic and leave full tool inventory to Technical + IT.
- “Leadership reporting” is weaker than “executive reporting dashboards” and overlaps with “analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it’s too generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value operational leadership and event delivery rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward scope and seniority: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more distinctive phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “Advocacy video production” to reflect recent leadership-level work.
- Consider swapping “Hybrid and virtual event production” for “Hybrid event production and livestream operations” to avoid repeating “production” and improve flow.
- If space allows, prioritize terms tied to recent roles: studio buildout, livestream operations, and event delivery over older hands-on editing language.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps heavily with Core Competencies (“Multimedia production and livestream operations”); differentiate or remove one.
- “PTZ camera systems” is quite tactical compared with the rest of the CV; keep only if targeting production-heavy roles.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since Drupal is the strongest recent platform in the experience section, this item should emphasize depth/order rather than breadth alone.

Suggested edit
- Reorder by demonstrated recent relevance: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Add light qualifiers only where they reinforce credibility without repeating other sections, e.g. “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; custom microsites)” if your format allows.
- If keeping this as a pure skills line, tighten to the most marketable platforms: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages” and drop GitHub Pages unless it is important for target roles.
- Keep platform names only here; save implementation detail for the coding/technical line and outcomes for work experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” especially Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages.
- Drupal accomplishments are already well covered in recent NACo roles; avoid restating them verbatim here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic coding terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API and tag implementation • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop versioned/basic terms (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) and consider removing “jQuery” unless it is still actively used in recent work or required by target roles.
- Rephrase “API integrations” to something more concrete if possible: “REST API integrations” or “front-end/API implementation.”
- If space allows, order by relevance/recency: JavaScript • REST API integrations • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • Google Tag Manager • HTML/CSS

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, and API integrations.
- GTM also overlaps conceptually with the analytics section; keep it here only if positioning it as implementation, not reporting.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize systems you actively build or use to run cross-team operations.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- Drop lower-value/older-feeling tools unless central to target roles: **Basecamp, Trello**
- If accurate, add light functional framing instead of a pure list: **Airtable-based workflow systems • Power Automate/Zapier integrations • Jira/Asana project operations • Slack/Teams collaboration**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in **Topline Skills**; keep this section tool-specific, not conceptual.
- Collaboration tools like **Slack** and **Teams** can feel low-signal on a senior CV unless tied to workflow/system ownership.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the scale/context shown elsewhere. It should signal enterprise email/engagement capability without repeating newsletter details already covered in work experience.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and modernize the list: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier for scope rather than outcomes: **Enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Keep platform names only here; let work experience carry metrics like “tens of thousands” and channel leadership

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding newsletter reach or campaign performance here; that duplicates the NACo roles
- “Multi-channel communications” and email leadership already appear in Core Competencies and Work Experience, so this item should stay tool-focused

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to show level of use or business impact. Since analytics is already emphasized in recent NACo roles, this item should be tighter and more differentiated.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic nouns with grouped capabilities: “GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • Executive dashboarding”
- Consider adding one qualifier if space allows: “enterprise reporting” or “behavior analytics” to signal seniority.
- If you can support it elsewhere, swap “A/B testing” for a more specific phrase like “conversion testing” or “performance analysis.”
- Keep the list to 6–8 items max; prioritize tools directly referenced in the 2022–Present roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider trimming one section or making this one more tool-only.
- “Dashboarding” overlaps with “reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and recent work bullets; “executive dashboarding” would be more distinct.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete outputs you can quantify.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team build and hands-on delivery: “Promoted through two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: size/timing of website refresh, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience/reach, email volume, or process improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence around 2–3 core contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and streamlined day-to-day publishing workflows.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “coordinated daily work with a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; frame this here as the launch/early production phase.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this at a tactical level, not strategic.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content for member-facing communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome: episode cadence, audience, internal adoption, or how the podcast supported advocacy/member engagement.
- Consider removing “contributed to” in favor of stronger verbs like “produced,” “developed,” or “launched.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad “digital content production” phrasing that repeats later digital/media roles; keep this entry centered on innovation/research support plus the first podcast launch.
- Don’t overstate multimedia leadership here, since later roles more credibly cover video, studio, and enterprise digital operations.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with stronger, more strategic multimedia claims elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, and keep production capabilities in experience/topline sections.

Suggested edit:
